summary: Roblox is a proprietary platform and also, by a wide margin, the best documented subject in this map: its creator documentation is open source, its engine reference and cloud interface descriptions ship with it, and its scripting language Luau is published separately under a permissive licence with its own site and a standalone runtime, making Luau the one Roblox artefact anyone else can simply pick up and use. One choice collides head-on with everything else here, and Roblox documents it precisely enough to be certain of: the unit of length is the stud, which Roblox converts to twenty-eight centimetres, its mass unit is 21.952 kilograms, and default gravity is 196.2 studs per second squared, which the same page converts to 54.936 metres per second squared, about five and a half times Earth, with Roblox listing 35 studs per second squared separately as the realistic value; the engine performs no unit conversion internally, so a scene authored in metres arrives both the wrong size and falling at the wrong rate, and neither error announces itself. Against that, Roblox is the only platform in this group that can write a neutral format at all: the importer reads FBX, glTF and plain object files, and a beta exporter writes glTF back out with meshes, textures, rigging, cages and facial pose data, though never animation, and only for assets the creator is permitted to take, so content goes in far more freely than it comes out. Two more results deserve a standards audience's attention: Roblox drives every headset through OpenXR, the immersive session standard, and its facial animation is built on the Facial Action Coding System with fifty published poses and seventeen required for marketplace items, which is a shared outside vocabulary rather than a private one. The walls are still walls: the place and model file formats have no published byte-level specification, the wire protocol is unpublished, interactivity never travels with an asset, and travel between places carries only data the client is allowed to read and never leaves the platform.
